Similar to the importance placed on feelings among SJWs, there's also a tendency for them to demand we listen to and trust their experience. The rationale behind this is that because the rest of us haven't had the same exact experience as them, we are unqualified to have an opinion and should therefore shut up and let them dictate the terms of our interactions.

I've started interpreting this as a deliberate attempt to subvert common sense and trick us into denying our own observations of the world. It's true, I can't truly know the experience of being a black man or the experience of being a woman. But does that render me incapable of rational thought? Fundamentally, we are humans and all individuals with an incredible range of experiences. Most of us understand what it's like to be called names, to feel fear, to feel joy. Most of us have interacted with tons of people who have experiences different from our own.

All that is to say, a woman's experience isn't some mystery box full of alien concepts that are impossible for me to wrap my male brain around. I can appreciate you have to deal with bullshit that is different from the bullshit I have to deal with. It is true, I don't get catcalled on the street. I'm not an idiot though and I can pretty much figure out what's going on there. I know what it's like to be sick of unwanted behavior directed towards you. I think most of us experience that kind of thing. Maybe we feel trapped in a psychologically abusive relationship and it takes a toll and feels emotionally draining. I would argue that's worse than catcalling -- even when you try to make catcalling sound more serious by claiming it has to do with rape culture.

We all understand what it is to struggle in the world. We all understand dealing with shitty people. We can't let people shut us out of conversations and vilify us just because of what we look like. This isn't a call to "stand up for white people" or anything like that. Rather, it is a call to stand up for intellectual honesty. The net result of "intersectionality" is people scrambling over themselves to figure out new ways they are oppressed. They do this because they recognize it is the current best way to have your opinion heard and valued and that's what all of us want. But they ways they leverage their social currency based around identity politics instead of intellectualism and good ideas is batshit insane.

Also, do not let them convince you of their own fragility. I had to develop a thick skin. Anyone else can too and if you can't then you don't have a place trying to convince me of anything. I'm a white guy. People talk shit about my people all day long and blame me for all the world's problems because I have a superficial resemblance to the people in power who actually run things and mess it up. But I'm not even complaining about that. I just let it roll of me. And it's not because my life is so great so I can take it. We can't assume any white guy's individual life is better or worse than yours. And in terms of discussing who has a right to an opinion, the important thing is it doesn't matter whose bullshit weighs the most. We all have to live here with each other. We all get to throw in our two cents.

I'd like to think of it as a compliment to my people but white guys are not magically the most psychologically resilient people around. Society expects us to be able to deal with any shit flung at us, so we do. I don't think it does anyone any favors to take those standards away. The correct path to equality isn't white men getting taken down a few pegs. It's not us shutting up so women can talk or black people can talk. It isn't a zero sum game. There's plenty of room at the top for everyone.
